prospect.name: Basel
prospect.occupation: Family business — elevator supply, installation and maintenance, plus real estate holdings. Personally runs a boutique hotel, Lemon Tree Residence, rated 9.2 on booking.com. Designated successor to his father.
prospect.family_status: Single, no children, hopes to have them
prospect.training_background: Calisthenics for roughly 14-15 months, three classes a week with a coach in groups of 5-10, and reports clear body-composition improvement from it. Currently attending only sporadically. Previously ran a disciplined meal-prep routine — five lunches, five breakfasts and five snacks cooked every Saturday. Was around 73 kg with a flat stomach in September/October of last year, now 80 kg.
prospect.medical: Collarbone pain when doing dips on a bar or rings, felt mainly on releasing the bar and recurring past six to eight reps. Previously severe enough that for a period of months he could only do dips with a resistance band for support. No other injuries. Chronic poor sleep since early June — consistently to bed between midnight and 3am.

signals: Anchored to a cheaper alternative that genuinely worked: 14 months of coached calisthenics with a real result — "My body shape is way better"
Explicitly comparison shopping before deciding: "I want to see what programs they have, and what pricing they also have, and just compare"
Named a price he considers fair, less than half the offer: "I was thinking maybe 2,000, 2,500... For six months, it felt fair"
Demanded written terms to evaluate against alternatives rather than buying on the call: "I still would need something concrete written, so I can make a fair comparison"

Alternative reading is the_optimizer — business owner, already lean and training, wants good to great on one body part — but that avatar assumes price reads as a quality signal, and here it read as a budget breach

goals.text: Lose the layer of belly fat — the rest of his physique he is happy with
Get healthier generally; believes the abdominal fat is affecting his testosterone
Add kettlebell work two days a week around his existing calisthenics without the two conflicting
Get his discipline and routine back to where it was last autumn
Look right — the stomach is the one part that does not match the rest of his body

pains.text: Discipline collapsed after a solo trip to Bosnia; now attends classes sporadically and skips when he wakes up unmotivated
Sleep is the stated root cause — to bed between midnight and 3am since early June, cannot make 7am classes
Diet slipped from a full meal-prep routine to eating out essentially every day; heavy carbs and restaurant seed oils
Hit a plateau after 14 months of calisthenics — gained about 7 kg back and cannot return to the flat stomach he had
Recurring collarbone pain on dips; previously months of being unable to do them unassisted
Post-trip identity conflict — no longer aligns with corporate life but is bound to run and inherit the family business, and raising it with his father "wasn't pretty"
Sedentary outside the training hour — very low non-exercise movement

objections.raw_quote: That's actually, that, it was, you it's way above my budget, to be honest. Okay. Yeah. I wasn't, no, I wasn't expecting it to be this much.
objections.rep_response: Ran the money play properly for once: isolated the objection ("apart from the finances, everything is good?"), asked what he had budgeted, gave the upfront-payment norm, framed plans as custom rather than fixed, and asked permission to open the finances. He never reached any of the financial-picture questions before the call was cut short.

objections.raw_quote: But the thing is, I was also planning to go see someone here, one-on-one, face-to-face, in person, that can help me. And I want to see what programs they have, and what pricing they also have, and just compare.
objections.rep_response: Said "That's fine", declined to provide anything in writing — "we haven't had anything that is written. Like, everything is super custom" — asked when the competing meetings were and began asking what else he would look for besides price, but was interrupted before an answer.

objections.raw_quote: Sorry about this, but I have to... We go in five minutes, so I would appreciate it if we can just wrap it up and- Let's get back to this conversation next week.
objections.rep_response: Accepted immediately and booked a follow-up for the same time on 7 July, confirming the prospect had received the calendar invite. No attempt to hold the frame or land a decision first — though an external interruption at the prospect's end forced the wrap.

tiers.note: "the full transformation to working with Trevor for the six months, it's 6k USD"

evidence: No decision either way; the price was met with "it's way above my budget" and then the conversation was cut short by an interruption at the prospect's end.
A specific follow-up was booked and confirmed: same time on 7 July, calendar invite sent and the prospect confirmed receipt — "Yeah, I have it."

Positive signal: full commitment given before price — "If we can figure out all the details and scheduling, are you fully committed to showing up and doing the work?" / "A hundred percent." And the programme itself landed cleanly — "it's just as I expected."
Counter-evidence: he intends to meet two local in-person trainers before deciding and asked for written terms to compare, which the rep declined to provide.
Counter-evidence: his own budget number is $2,000-2,500, less than half the offer, and no financial-picture work was done to close that gap.
outcome.next_step: Follow-up call booked for 7 July 2026 at the same time; invite confirmed received. Prospect to meet two local in-person trainers first and compare.

notable.note: The strongest discovery in this batch and the weakest consequence work — the rep never asked what happens if nothing changes, so the $6,000 landed with no cost-of-inaction behind it. He also opened a large identity thread and dropped it: the prospect volunteered a post-trip crisis about the family business, his father, and wanting to leave city life, and none of it was connected to the training decision. Two things a principal should see: the rep told a 14-month calisthenics practitioner that calisthenics "is not burning fat", and he refused to provide anything in writing to a prospect who explicitly asked in order to comparison shop.
